primary_conclusion: The archived positive morphology-phylogeny association is not robust. It becomes weakly negative and non-significant after feature-orientation correction, and remains non-significant in a standardized-sequence sensitivity analysis.
causal_diagnostic: The raw-as-stored pipeline closely recovers the archived correlation, whereas orientation correction collapses the anomalous Brugmansia branch. This pattern is consistent with the reverse-oriented Brugmansia matK record driving much of the archived positive association.
claim_boundary: This does not establish absence of evolutionary signal. Six taxa and two plastid markers provide limited information and low statistical power.
